title: An IN filter argument overwrites the existing filter on the column like any predicate
query: DEFINE MEASURE Sales[Blue Green Sales] = CALCULATE ( [Sales Amount], 'Product'[Color] IN { "Blue", "Green" } )
EVALUATE SUMMARIZECOLUMNS ( 'Product'[Color], "Blue Green Sales", [Blue Green Sales] )

source.quote: You can use any condition as an argument, as long as it can
source.supports: the page's second example uses Product[Color] IN { "Red", "Blue" } and shows the same value on every color row

source.quote: A filter argument overrides the existing corresponding filters over the same column(s), unless it is embedded within KEEPFILTERS
source.supports: the filter overrides the row's filter on Color

derivation: Blue sales are rows 4, 6 = 50 + 30 = 80; Green has none. The IN filter replaces each row's color: 80 on all three rows.
notes: SUM of a fixed decimal (currency) column is taken to be a fixed decimal, as in the seed cases.
